identity.description: Mean of the last k observations, held flat over the horizon. The family's second floor and its resident SMOOTHER: as a forecaster it is the level-only reference for non-seasonal series; as a preprocessor it emits the rolling-mean series itself for a downstream forecaster to consume.

consumes.note: regular time-indexed numeric series with at least k trailing observations

emits.note: floor role: the last k-window mean repeated flat across the horizon; no native intervals
smoother role: the full rolling-mean series, consumable by a downstream forecaster or detrender — the composition role that distinguishes sma from seasonal_naive

learnsVsFixed.note: nothing is estimated — the window mean is arithmetic on the last k values; the window length is supplied configuration. Reusable as a fixed floor/smoother on any numeric series.

window.note: k, the only knob — a CONFIG choice (bias-variance of the smoother), searchable in the smoother role but conventionally FIXED in the floor role so the reference does not move

invariances.why: the arithmetic mean is equivariant to rescaling; forecasts and smoothed series rescale with the input
by Jensen's inequality mean(f(y)) != f(mean(y)) for nonlinear monotone f — unlike seasonal_naive, averaging does NOT commute with transforms
a NaN inside the window poisons the mean (or silently shrinks the effective window under skipna) — the grid must be gap-free
the mean is only defined on numeric values
no distributional form — only the implicit bet that the recent local level persists, which is a structural (not distributional) premise
needs only k observations — with seasonal_naive, the cheapest history requirement in the family
any horizon receives the same flat last-window mean — it lags a trend by construction ((k-1)/2 steps) and never extends one

featureStats.why: the k-window mean lags a trend by (k-1)/2 steps, so a strong slope makes the flat forecast systematically biased — the stat that routes trending series away from this floor
a window spanning a seasonal cycle averages the seasonality away, so strong seasonality means the honest floor is seasonal_naive, not sma
averaging k points cuts noise variance by ~1/k — the exact payoff that justifies sma in its smoother role upstream of another forecaster

modelMetrics.why: even a floor is scored on the family scoreboard: on seasonal series sma loses to seasonal_naive by construction, and that ranking honestly decides which floor a given series should be scored against

edgeCases.note: shrink the window or fall back to last-value naive

edgeCases.behavior: NaN (or a silently shorter window) in the forecast
seasonality averaged away; flat forecast misses every peak
edgeCases.note: route to seasonal_naive or a seasonal model

edgeCases.behavior: the mean is dragged by a single spike for k periods
edgeCases.note: a median window or longer k is the robust alternative

driver.constructor: no fit — forecast: y.rolling(window=k).mean().iloc[-1] tiled over the horizon; smoother: the full rolling-mean series
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter: (time_col, value_col, freq, horizon) + window config; dual-role wrapper exposes forecast(horizon) and transform() -> smoothed series

placementClaims.why: the trailing window must be gap-free or the mean is poisoned; time-aware fill first
averaging on a variance-stabilized (log) scale resists spikes — the raw-scale mean is spike-sensitive, and since averaging does not commute with transforms this is a real choice
single numeric series has nothing to encode
